query: Which material can be used for enhanced catalytic activity and durability toward HER and HOR, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A hierarchically nanostructured Ni-based alloy electrode prepared by partial dealloying and/or templated etching can achieve enhanced catalytic activity and prolonged durability for both hydrogen evolution (HER) and hydrogen oxidation (HOR).
generation.material_initial_state: A Ni-based alloy substrate (e.g., Ni-Al or Ni-Cu) in a fully alloyed state prior to selective etching/dealloying.
generation.intervention: Subject the alloy to a controlled dealloying or templated etching process to remove less noble components and create a stable, high-surface-area nanoporous microstructure.
generation.conditions: Perform dealloying in acidic or alkaline solutions under electrochemical potential control, then evaluate the resulting electrode for HER and HOR in standard electrochemical cells over multiple cycles.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of interconnected pores, channels, and catalytic nanofacets throughout the Ni-based scaffold, which increase the density of active sites and support stable operation.
generation.mechanism: Abundant active sites on the nanoporous Ni-based surface improve kinetics of hydrogen adsorption and desorption, while the durable Ni framework with possible minor alloying additions (e.g., Fe, Mo) maintains mechanical integrity and chemical stability in aggressive electrochemical conditions.
generation.predicted_outcome: Significant improvements in HER/HOR activity (lower onset potentials and higher currents at fixed overpotentials) and enhanced structural longevity compared with conventional Ni or similar catalysts without nanostructuring.
generation.baseline: Unstructured Ni or Pt-based materials with either lower intrinsic activity at equal loading or less stable performance under prolonged cycling in acidic or alkaline media.
generation.boundary: Optimal performance depends on the controlled design of nanoporous layer thickness, pore size, and choice of minor alloying elements. Performance in extremely corrosive solutions or under high current densities still requires further validation.
generation.uncertainty: No direct data in the provided records confirm the exact magnitude of performance improvement or the synergy of specific alloying additions, so further experimental validation is needed.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate nano-architected Ni-based catalysts by partial dealloying of Ni-X alloys, then measure HER and HOR activity in acidic vs. alkaline solutions over extended cycling periods.
measurements: Electrochemical impedance and exchange current density
Structural and compositional analysis pre- and post-testing
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the tested nanoporous Ni-based catalysts do not show reliably increased catalytic current and stability relative to a reference Ni or Pt-based catalyst under identical conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.

decision.trend: None of the cited works addresses electrocatalytic activity or durability under HER/HOR conditions. The available papers focus on high-entropy alloys and superalloys primarily for mechanical performance and oxidation resistance, leaving a gap in catalytic studies for hydrogen reactions.
decision.unsolved: A dedicated approach to designing or adapting these advanced alloys (or related materials) for enhanced electrocatalytic performance in hydrogen evolution and oxidation—especially under extended service conditions—has not yet been reported in this literature set.
decision.lever: Develop a nanoporous or hierarchically textured Ni-based interface (e.g., via dealloying or templated etching) to maximize electrochemically active surface area and improve mass transport, while preserving bulk mechanical integrity.
decision.why: By architecting a high-surface-area framework on a robust Ni-based substrate, both catalytic activity (via abundant active sites) and longevity (via stable support) can be enhanced under the electrochemical stresses of HER and HOR, matching the question’s requirement for improved activity and durability without changing the bulk composition.
